_comment: The three alerts of lane Q14 alerts-that-cannot-fire, exactly as they shipped at 11e6f88ce3773dd1819c1d4c9c01c0ee084aba6b (build 4078). Captured from git show by script, not hand-typed: make-fixture.py for the first two and make-fixture-fix2.py for integrity_check_overdue (the project's private evidence archive, evidence/alerts-that-cannot-fire-2026-09-18/builder/ and fix2/edits/). connection_count divides by SERVERPROPERTY('MaxConnections'), which is not a property, so its value is always NULL; sql_response_time's query returns two result sets and the evaluator reads the first, the constant 1; integrity_check_overdue reads only DATABASEPROPERTYEX(name, 'LastGoodCheckDbTime'), which is NULL for every database on SQL Server 14.0.2130.4, so it answers 0 there.

alerts.name: SQL Server Response Time
alerts.description: SQL Server response time to a probe query is high
alerts.query: DECLARE @t DATETIME = GETDATE(); SELECT 1; SELECT DATEDIFF(MILLISECOND, @t, GETDATE()) AS value

alerts.name: User Connections High
alerts.description: User connection count approaching the configured maximum
alerts.query: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS FLOAT) * 100.0 / NULLIF(CAST(SERVERPROPERTY('MaxConnections') AS FLOAT), 0) AS value FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions WHERE is_user_process = 1

alerts.name: Integrity Check Overdue
alerts.description: No DBCC CHECKDB has been run within the threshold period
alerts.query: SELECT ISNULL(MAX(DATEDIFF(HOUR, CONVERT(DATETIME, DBCC_LastKnownGood), GETDATE())), 0) AS value FROM (SELECT d.name, DATABASEPROPERTYEX(d.name, 'LastGoodCheckDbTime') AS DBCC_LastKnownGood FROM sys.databases d WHERE d.database_id > 4 AND d.state = 0) x WHERE DBCC_LastKnownGood IS NOT NULL
